title: Exterior and interior handover checklists
audience: Car detailers who complete the handover of an exterior and interior detail, and who need a record the owner can check.
learningOutcomes: Complete an exterior checklist covering painted surfaces, the engine compartment, wheels and tyres, critical details and glass.
Complete an interior checklist covering hard surfaces, leather and fabric, glass and mirrors.
Record items that are not finished, and why, rather than ticking them.

instruction.heading: Why the checklist is the evidence
instruction.body: A checklist turns a finished job into a record that someone else can check. The detailing checklist in the source set is organised into exterior and interior sections, with a box for each item and a comment line at the end of each section. Use it as the basis for the handover, alongside the condition map from the intake record. Its purpose is not to show that everything was perfect, but to show what was done, what was not done, and why. A tick against an item that was not completed is worse than a blank, because it is a false record. Complete the checklist at handover, in good light, with the vehicle in the state the owner will see it.

instruction.heading: Exterior items
instruction.body: The exterior section covers the painted surface: contaminants removed, metallic fallout and acid-rain spotting removed, marks treated to the level agreed, residues removed, and a final finish evenly applied. The engine compartment section records whether contaminants were removed from the engine, the compartment and the inner bonnet, and whether the engine was dressed. Wheels, tyres and wheel wells are checked as cleaned and, where agreed, dressed. Critical details include the grille, air dam and bumpers; the door, boot and fuel-cap jambs; rubber and vinyl trim; and the exterior glass and mirrors. Check each item against the work order that was agreed, not against what the detailer would like to achieve. Where the agreed scope excludes an item, mark it as not in scope rather than complete.

instruction.heading: Interior items
instruction.body: The interior section has two parts: hard vinyl, rubber and glass surfaces, and leather and fabric surfaces. Hard surfaces include the dashboard, console and instrument panel, which are dressed; the steering wheel, foot pedals and vinyl seats, which are not dressed; the glove box and storage areas; door-frame weather-stripping; interior glass and mirrors; the rear window deck; and the ashtrays. Leather and fabric surfaces are cleaned while damp, not saturated, and the same areas are checked. The checklist separates dressed from not dressed, and the difference matters. The steering wheel and pedals are left undressed, because a dressing on them creates a slip risk for the driver. Check the pedals and wheel by touch before handover.

instruction.heading: Exceptions, comments and sign-off
instruction.body: Use the comment line for each exception, with its reason. For example: a loose trim piece not touched, under the exception plan; a cracked lens masked and not treated; a stain that did not come out and is recorded with the owner's agreement. Record the owner's sign-off on the completed checklist, and record the permission for any photographs. Take handover photographs in shade and under a directional light, so the record shows the true state. A precise handover record also helps when a customer returns with a question, because the file shows the condition at handover rather than a recollection of it.

procedure: Open the checklist for this job alongside the work order and the intake record.
Walk the exterior in shade, and check each painted, engine, wheel and detail item against the agreed scope.
Mark each item as complete, not complete, or not in scope, and add a comment for each exception.
Check the interior in the same way, and check the steering wheel and pedals by touch.
Check interior glass and mirrors in good light.
Take handover photographs with permission, in shade.
Obtain the owner's sign-off, and file the checklist with the job record.

workedExamples.situation: On the exterior checklist, the inside of the rear window is streaky, and a bumper scuff remains that the owner agreed to leave untreated.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you mark the checklist?
workedExamples.reasoning: Mark the rear glass as not complete, with the reason and the step still needed, or re-clean it before handover if time allows. Mark the bumper scuff as not in scope, referencing the agreed work order and the owner's acceptance. Do not tick either item as complete.

workedExamples.situation: On the interior checklist, residue from a drink is still on the steering wheel. The owner is in a hurry.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Mark it not complete, describe the residue and its location, and note that the item is not dressed. Clean the residue without dressing it if possible, and check it by touch. If residue remains, record it as remaining, with the owner's sign-off on that record.

equipmentAndPpe: Checklist, printed or digital, for this job.
Directional torch for dark areas, and good light for the glass.
Camera, used with the owner's permission.
PPE: normal work clothing and closed footwear (see “Manual handling, wet floors and site hygiene” for slip controls).

commonErrors.error: Ticking items that were not done.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark the item not complete and write the reason.

commonErrors.error: Dressing the steering wheel or the pedals.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave those areas undressed, as the checklist states.

commonErrors.error: Completing the checklist after the owner has left.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete it at handover, with the owner present where possible.
Photograph in shade under a directional light, with permission.
Write the reason and the owner's agreement on every exception.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Photographs can show the owner's property and personal items. The OAIC notes that the Privacy Act generally does not apply to businesses with annual turnover of $3 million or less, but applies to some regardless of turnover. Use photographs only for the job record, with permission, and store them securely.
Leaving dressing off the steering wheel and pedals is a safety control, because a slippery surface on a driver's controls is a hazard. This is working practice, not a stated legal requirement.

qualityStandard: Every item on the exterior and interior checklist is marked complete, not complete, or not in scope.
Each exception has a comment with the reason and the owner's agreement.
Steering wheel and pedals are checked by touch and left undressed.
documentationEvidence: Checklist signed or dated, with the owner's sign-off.
Handover photographs taken with permission, and the record of exceptions.
summary: A checklist is evidence only when every item is marked honestly.
Record each exception with its reason and the owner's agreement.
Leave the steering wheel and pedals undressed, and check them by touch.

knowledgeChecks.question: An item within the agreed scope is not finished at handover. How is it marked?
options: Ticked, because the owner will not notice the gap at handover
Marked not complete, with the reason written beside it
Left blank with no comment, since the item is almost finished
Removed from the checklist so it is not shown in the record

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are the steering wheel and foot pedals left undressed?
options: Dressing is too expensive for the owner to pay
They are made of metal and need a special polish to look good
The owner asked for it, so the detailer dresses them anyway
A dressing on them creates a slip risk for the driver

knowledgeChecks.question: When should handover photographs be taken?
options: In direct midday sun, to show the gloss on the paint in full
In shade and under a directional light, with the owner's permission
Only if the owner asks for them after the job is handed back
After the owner has driven away, so the photos are not disturbed
